draft.title: Element symbols and compounds
card: Each element has a symbol of one or two letters. The first letter is a capital and the second, if there is one, is small. Carbon is C and calcium is Ca.
Some symbols come from older names, often Latin. Sodium is Na and iron is Fe.
A compound is made of two or more different elements joined together. Its formula shows which elements are in it.
A small number after a symbol tells how many atoms of that element are in the formula. In CO2 there is one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. With no number, there is one atom.
draft.remember: A symbol names an element. A formula uses symbols and small numbers to show what a compound is made of.

a.q: Which formula shows a compound with one sulfur atom and three oxygen atoms?
a.why: S is sulfur and O is oxygen. The small number 3 after O gives three oxygen atoms, and no number after S means one sulfur atom. S3O has the numbers on the wrong atoms.
a.clue: The small number goes after the symbol it counts.

b.q: Dani reads the formula CaCO3 on a bag of garden lime. Which statement about CaCO3 is correct?
opts: It is a compound with three elements, and three oxygen atoms
It is an element with two letters in its symbol
It is a compound with two elements, and three calcium atoms
It is a compound with three elements, and three carbon atoms
b.why: Ca, C and O are three different elements, so CaCO3 is a compound. Only O has a small 3, so there are three oxygen atoms. Ca is one symbol of two letters, not C and a separate a.
b.clue: Split the formula at each capital letter.

b.best: It is a compound with three elements, and three oxygen atoms
